policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Orthographic/morphological variation of the same present infinitive (συνιστάνειν / συνιστᾶν); ASV 'to commend ourselves' renders either identically and no note is mapped here.

ASV renders the second clause as a disjunctive question, 'or need we, as do some, epistles of commendation', which is ἢ; the RP conditional Εἰ ('if we need') would have produced a conditional clause, not 'or'.

ASV has one 'of commendation' governing both phrases, 'epistles of commendation to you or from you'; English would not repeat the adjective for the RP second συστατικῶν, so the wording does not distinguish the readings and no note is mapped here.
Word order only: both readings contain the same words (ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτῶν ἱκανοί ἐσμεν), and English clause order in 'we are sufficient of ourselves' is fixed by English syntax, not by the Greek sequence.
Orthographic variation of the same reflexive pronoun (αὑτῶν / ἑαυτῶν); ASV 'as from ourselves' renders either identically.
The ASV note 'Greek in letters.' glosses 'written' with a plural noun, matching the dative plural γράμμασιν; the Treg singular γράμματι would have been glossed 'in letter'.

The ASV note 'Greek in.' glosses 'engraven on stones', stating that the Greek word behind 'on' is the preposition 'in'; that presupposes ἐν λίθοις, which only the RP reading supplies — the base has the bare dative λίθοις with no preposition to gloss.

ASV text 'the ministration of condemnation hath glory' renders the dative τῇ διακονίᾳ (glory belonging to the ministration), and the mapped textual_variant note assigns the nominative construction, 'the ministration of condemnation is glory' (ἡ διακονία), to 'many ancient authorities' — i.e. to the reading the ASV did not follow.
ASV 'exceed in glory' renders either the bare dative δόξῃ or RP's ἐν δόξῃ; English requires 'in' for the dative of respect regardless, and the verse's only mapped note concerns v008.
Orthographic variation of the same preposition (εἵνεκεν / ἕνεκεν); ASV 'by reason of' renders either identically.

ASV 'a veil upon his face' renders the simple αὐτοῦ and the reflexive ἑαυτοῦ alike, since English 'his' with a coreferential subject is unmarked; both notes are alternative_rendering and do not bear on the pronoun.

ASV 'until this very day' must supply the noun 'day' for RP's τῆς σήμερον as well as for the fuller τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας; 'very' is emphasis, not evidence of a second Greek word, and no note is mapped here.

ASV text reads 'it not being revealed to them that it is done away in Christ' — the conjunction ὅτι introducing the content clause. The relative ὅ τι would give 'which is done away', which the ASV prints only in the margin as an alternative_rendering ('which veil is done away'), not in the text.

ASV 'whensoever Moses is read' renders the indefinite temporal clause ἡνίκα ἂν ἀναγινώσκηται with ἄν plus subjunctive; the RP indicative ἀναγινώσκεται without ἄν would give a definite 'when Moses is read'. The same 'whensoever' answers ἄν plus subjunctive in the next verse.

Both readings are ἄν with the subjunctive, differing only in whether the particle is written ἐὰν or elided δ[ὲ] ἂν; ASV 'But whensoever it shall turn' renders either identically, and the sole note is alternative_rendering about the unexpressed subject.

ASV 'where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty' does not settle ἐκεῖ: English idiom supplies the correlative 'there' after a 'where' clause and needs 'is' for the verbless Greek clause, so the base reading yields the same wording. The 'there' is not italicized as a supply and no note is mapped here.
